free_tier.stated: No free tier in use: 'All of our premium packages support posting, but some servers are read-only (free.xsusenet.com is no longer in use).'
free_tier.notes: No price quoted; the pricing page was not read.

per_object_cap.stated: Not published; the unit is the article.

egress.terms: Plan-based; the only ceiling named on the page read is the connection count.

interface_detail: NNTP reader, standard commands; the page lists the full refusal set a client meets at connect and at article fetch.
chaining: A shorter-retention spool is the wrong primary for a 1 TiB/month archive and the right fill for recent content; 1100 days is the only day count among the providers in this set that publishes one.

limits.value: 'Too Many Connections' is a named refusal; the plan's connection count is the ceiling
posting is allowed on premium packages and refused with '440 Posting Not Allowed' where it is not

limits_note: This is the only provider in the set whose documentation lists the connection-level refusals next to the article-level ones, which is what a client needs to tell 'wrong password' from 'article gone'.
binding_note: At 1100 days the spool is the shortest published retention here, so a client pulling older releases meets 430 far more often than a connection or byte limit.

identity_cost.detail: Paid client-area account with email and card; usenet credentials are separate from the client-area login, which the KB calls out explicitly.

reliability_note: Nothing past 1100 days exists on this spool; the KB warns that client-area credentials are not usenet credentials, which is a common first-hour failure; a 503 is an overload rather than a credential problem.
confidence_note: Every string and the retention figure are the vendor's own knowledge-base page. No probe was run.

evidence.proved: The refusal set: '502 Authentication Error / 482 Invalid username or password'; '440 Posting Not Allowed'; '480 Authentication Required'; '423 Bad Article Number or 430 No Such Article Found' with 'Our retention is limited to 1100 days'; '503 Service Unavailable ... possibly due to maintenance or overload'; 'Too Many Connections'. Also 'Your email address and password for our client area are NOT your Usenet credentials.'
Connection-count sizing: 'Set connections to what your plan actually allows ... Going over what the plan permits gets connections refused.'

notes: Candidates for the first failure: the connection cap, the 1100-day wall, or the credential split between client area and NNTP. The credential split is the one that breaks a first-hour setup; the 1100-day wall is the one that breaks an archive pull. Both are documented.

extras.failure_angle: credential split and a published retention wall
extras.account_states: 482 invalid credentials or expired account ('ensure your account is still active and hasn't expired'); 480 auth required; 503 service unavailable; 440 posting refused
